\par\smallskip{\footnotesize\raggedright\textit{Note.} Retention: per matched clean control, the share of gold valid-claim signatures that appear anywhere on the supported side (a lenient metric), averaged over controls; the difference is C4 minus C2 on controls parseable under both, with a case-level bootstrap 95\% CI (B = 10000) \citep{efron1979bootstrap}. For qwen3:30b-a3b every paired difference is 0, so no interval is reported, although 26/72 of its controls had supported-side items changed. Supported-side items: mean per case over all 144 cases (unparseable artifacts count as 0). The baselines are post hoc and exploratory: they transform the frozen C2 artifacts and rescore them with the frozen scorer (S and the grid: means over seeds 1, 2, 3); the readouts hold for this grid and these seeds only. S relabels or deletes a fraction of supported-side items chosen by position and seed only; ``at C4's attrition'' interpolates the S curve at C4's supported items per case. Non-decision families: the five families other than decision (60 risk and 60 control cases); for qwen3:30b-a3b, C2 and C4 differ there by 2 cases only. Grid: 81 configurations per model of S, R (downgrade of supported requirements) and X (reset of decision-boundary fields and deletion of interview-signal risks, checklist and limitation items). Source-type policies (4; designed after it was known that all bait sources are notes) move supported-side items that cite a note (and, in two of them, items without a source ID), optionally followed by X with $r=1$; they read only source types and item source IDs and are not content-blind. Best policy: lowest trap-failure rate among the four.\par}
